name: D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones
life_summary: David Martyn Lloyd-Jones was born in Cardiff in 1899. He grew up in Llangeitho, Cardiganshire, and moved with his family to London in 1914. He trained in medicine at St Bartholomew's Hospital, worked from 1921 as an assistant to the royal physician Sir Thomas Horder, and gained an MD in 1923 and the MRCP in 1925 before leaving medicine for the ministry in 1926. He married Dr Bethan Phillips in January 1927 and from February 1927 was minister of the Forward Movement church at Sandfields, Aberavon, where their daughters Elizabeth and Ann were born. In September 1938 he began at Westminster Chapel, London, alongside G. Campbell Morgan, committed to London in April 1939, and became sole minister when Morgan retired in 1943. There he preached long expository series, including Ephesians and Romans, helped start the Puritan Conference in 1950, and in October 1966 publicly urged evangelicals to leave mixed denominations. After major surgery in 1968 he retired from Westminster Chapel and spent his last years editing sermons for publication, lecturing and chairing the trustees of London Theological Seminary, and he died at his home in Ealing on 1 March 1981.

phases.label: Childhood in Cardiff, Llangeitho
phases.summary: Born in Cardiff, the second of three sons of a grocer. From spring 1906 the family lived in Llangeitho, Cardiganshire, where he attended the village school and Tregaron County School.

phases.label: London medical years
phases.summary: After the family moved to London he attended Marylebone Grammar School (1914-1917), trained in medicine at St Bartholomew's Hospital, worked from 1921 as assistant to Sir Thomas Horder, and gained an MD (1923) and the MRCP (1925). According to the Dictionary of Welsh Biography he was converted in his early twenties, and in 1926 he left medicine to prepare for the ministry.

phases.label: Sandfields, Aberavon pastorate
phases.summary: Minister of Bethlehem Forward Movement Church (Sandfields) in Aberavon, Port Talbot, a Presbyterian Church of Wales mission, where he and Bethan raised daughters Elizabeth (born 1927) and Ann (born 1937). In July-August 1932 he preached in Toronto, Canada.

phases.label: Associate at Westminster Chapel
phases.summary: Began at Westminster Chapel in September 1938 on a temporary basis, then committed to London in April 1939 as associate minister to G. Campbell Morgan; in 1939 he also became president of the Inter-Varsity Fellowship. During the Blitz the family lived in Haslemere, Surrey, while he continued to minister at the chapel.

phases.label: Sole minister, Westminster Chapel
phases.summary: As sole minister of Westminster Chapel he preached expository series including Ephesians (Sunday mornings, 1954-1962), Romans (Friday evenings, October 1955 to March 1968) and Acts (Sunday evenings, 1965-1968). The period ended with major surgery in March 1968 and his retirement that year.

phases.label: Retirement and wider ministry
phases.summary: After retiring he edited his sermons for publication and spoke at conferences, including 1969 lectures on preaching at Westminster Theological Seminary, Philadelphia; from 1977 he chaired the trustees of London Theological Seminary. He preached for the last time in June 1980 and died at his Ealing home in March 1981.

corrections: June 1944 event: the 1980 interview does not tie the ~300 figure to the bombing; corrected to say the flying bomb blew off half the roof and about 150 people met in a borrowed hall for 14 weeks.
Horder event: changed 'By 1921' to '1921' (MLJ Trust says he started work as Horder's assistant in 1921) and replaced the Wikipedia source with the Dictionary of Welsh Biography.

Removed the '30 May 1968 retirement letter' event: the date and wording are supported only by Wikipedia, and no independent source could be found; replaced with a 1968 retirement event sourced to the Dictionary of Welsh Biography and Banner of Truth.

1932 Toronto event: 'first transatlantic trip' is not stated in any fetched source, so it was removed; dated July-August 1932 per the Dictionary of Welsh Biography. The Evangelical Magazine source (which gives no year) was replaced with DWB.
Sandfields phase: removed the Evangelical Magazine source and the unconfirmed 'first transatlantic trip' wording.
Associate phase: Haslemere is now sourced to a fetched Christian Today article instead of the CT 1980 interview, which does not mention Haslemere; wording changed to 'during the Blitz'.
Fire event: added the detail given by DWB that Martyn was thrown from an upstairs window to neighbours.
Added a Spring 1906 event for the move to Llangeitho (DWB).
Marriage event: added the venue, Charing Cross Chapel (DWB).
1943 event: replaced the Banner of Truth source with DWB, which explicitly dates Morgan's retirement to 1943.
March 1968 event: reworded to say he faced major surgery that month, which by his own account led him to leave Westminster Chapel, matching the interview.
Death event: added the funeral at Bethel Chapel, Newcastle Emlyn (DWB).
Harold: specified 'elder brother', because Martyn was the second of three sons.
life_summary: added the 1921 Horder date, the April 1939 commitment and the 1950 and October 1966 dates, and removed the unverified 'advising ministers' claim.
